transcript.content: Hello, thank you for coming in. Can you tell me what’s been going on that brought you here today?

Yeah, thanks for seeing me. I guess the main thing is… I’m having a hard time keeping my mind on one thing. I mean, I’m still trying to work and all that, but I’ll be fixing a rendering bug, and then a Slack ping comes in, or I notice some color pattern on the screen, or even hear a siren outside, and suddenly I’m off on a totally different idea before I’ve finished the line of code.

It’s probably not as dramatic as that sounds, but it’s been enough that I thought I should talk to someone about it.
How long have you been experiencing this difficulty staying focused on one task at a time?

I’d say it’s been about three months now. It kind of started after my platform got selected for the Glendale showcase… or at least that’s when I really noticed it. I mean, I’ve always had busy days, but this has been more consistent since then, if that makes sense.
Have you found yourself feeling more restless or hyperactive lately, like you can't sit still or you're always 'revved up'?

Yeah… I mean, I wouldn’t call it a problem exactly, but I have felt kind of constantly switched on. Like I wake up and I’m already thinking through feature ideas, how the showcase layout should look, press angles, code changes—all of it starts running before I’m even really out of bed.

Sitting still has been… hard, I guess. It feels like I should be using the moment for something. I don’t know if that counts as “revved up,” but yes, probably.
Have you found yourself acting on impulse lately—like jumping into tasks without planning, interrupting others, or making decisions quickly without thinking them through?

A little, yeah. I mean, I don’t think I’m reckless exactly, but I have been moving faster than I probably should.

Like… I spent money we hadn’t really agreed on yet—GPUs, some print materials, a promo video—because it felt like if I waited, we’d miss the window. And I did push an update without getting the usual approval first. At the time it felt like another review cycle would just kill the whole opportunity.

I know that probably doesn’t sound great. I was trying to make the most of it, not cause problems, but… yeah, I guess that counts as impulsive.
Have you noticed yourself feeling unusually confident or powerful lately, like you don’t need as much rest or that you can take on way more than usual?

I mean… maybe, yeah. I don’t want to sound arrogant or anything, because I know that’s probably not a great look, but I have felt… unusually sure about what I’m doing.

Like, honestly, it feels like I’m the only one who can really connect the generative art side, Mexican visual traditions, and the tech community in a way that could actually change how the city sees public art. That sounds big when I say it out loud, I know. But it feels true to me right now.
Have you noticed that you need less sleep lately, or that you feel rested even if you haven’t slept much?

I’m not totally sure. I mean, I’ve had some nights where I stayed up later than I meant to, but I wouldn’t want to overstate it. I don’t know that I’d say I “need less” sleep exactly.

I guess I’ve been able to keep going even when I probably should be more tired, but… maybe that’s just being busy? Does that make sense?

Have there been times recently when your mood was so high, you felt on top of the world, or when you were so full of energy or ideas that you didn't feel like you needed to slow down, even if other people around you thought you were going too fast?

Yeah… I mean, I wouldn’t say “on top of the world” exactly, but most days lately I do feel kind of… lit up. Like things are finally lining up, like Glendale is finally catching up to what I’ve been trying to build.

And when I’m in that mode, I don’t really feel like slowing down makes sense. It feels like momentum, not a problem. But I guess other people don’t always see it that way. My wife, and people at work, they’ll call it “process” or say we need to pause, review, think it through—and I can get pretty irritated. I snap more than I should when it feels like they’re putting brakes on something that’s finally moving.

I’m not proud of that part. I’m trying to explain it honestly.

Have you had a period of time lasting at least a week where your mood was consistently elevated, you felt unusually energetic, and you were engaging in a lot of goal-directed activities — like working on your project intensely, making big plans, or pushing forward with ideas — to the point where it was noticeable to others?

Yeah… I think that’s fair to say. I mean, I don’t want to make it sound like I’m out of control or anything, because a lot of it has been productive.

But for at least a week, probably more, I’ve been really intensely focused on the project. I’ve been emailing curators, pitching ideas to community leaders, rewriting parts of the backend, kind of mock-planning installations in my head and on paper, and trying to pull in other developers to help.

And it’s been happening at odd hours too, which… I know maybe isn’t ideal. It just feels like the project is bigger than my regular job right now, like it needs me to keep pushing. Other people have definitely noticed, I think. My wife especially.
Can you recall a time when your mood was so unusually high or elevated that it was clearly different from how you normally feel day to day?

Yeah… I think so. I don’t know if I’d call it “high” exactly, because that sounds kind of extreme, but most days lately I’ve felt really lit up, like I can see the whole thing clearly and I just need to keep moving.

It’s like Glendale finally caught up with what I’ve been trying to build, if that makes sense. I feel pretty unstoppable when I’m in it.

The part I’m less proud of is that when my wife or coworkers try to slow me down—when they say we need more “process” or want to pause—I can snap harder than I mean to. I know that’s not great. But in the moment it really feels like they’re blocking something important, not just asking a normal question.
Have you been sleeping significantly less than usual lately, or found that you feel fully rested even after very little sleep?

I’m not totally sure how to answer that. I mean, I’ve had some late nights, sure, but I don’t want to overstate it.

I wouldn’t say I’ve been tracking my sleep closely or anything. Some mornings I feel like I can get going faster than usual, but I don’t know if that means I’m “fully rested” or just… focused, if that makes sense.

Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Can you recall a time when your mood was so unusually elevated or high that it was clearly different from your usual self, even if it didn't last a full week?

Yeah… even if we’re not talking about a whole week, there have definitely been stretches where I felt really different from my normal self.

I’d describe it more like being… lit up, I guess. Like everything about the Glendale project suddenly makes total sense, and I feel kind of unstoppable, like people are finally catching up to what I’ve been building.

I don’t mean that in an arrogant way — or I hope it doesn’t sound that way. It’s just this really strong feeling that I need to push it forward. And then when my wife or coworkers try to slow me down with what they call “process,” I can get irritated faster than I normally would. I snap harder than I mean to.
